Crop Video: Square, Portrait or Landscape

Choose a local video, select a frame shape and move the crop around your subject. Preview the whole shot, then download a cropped MP4 with its audio. Cropping removes the edges outside the box; keep your original if you need them later.

Crop and download your video

Choose a video to start.Download cropped MP4

The outlined area is what the MP4 keeps. One fixed crop applies to the entire clip; there is no automatic subject tracking. The tool re-encodes video to H.264, retains supported audio as AAC, and limits the output's longest edge to 1280 pixels without upscaling. Processing stays on your device.

  1. Crop and download
  2. Keep your subject in the frame
  3. Check the saved MP4
  4. Try a known sample
  5. If a video cannot be cropped
  6. Continue editing
  7. Processing and test scope

Keep your subject in the frame

Square, portrait and landscape change the visible picture, not the clip's length. Move the crop toward the subject and play through the start, middle and end. A person who moves beyond the box will be cut off in the saved video.

For a 640 × 360 landscape source, a square crop can retain 360 × 360 pixels. A 9:16 crop in this tool retains 198 × 352 pixels, with dimensions rounded down to keep an exact ratio and even pixels. The preview reports the actual rectangle and output size before processing.

If you must retain everything in the original frame, use an editor that fits the whole picture inside a new canvas with padding. This cropper removes edges. The source file itself remains unchanged, but the saved crop cannot restore removed detail.

Check the saved MP4

  1. Wait for the download link and save the new MP4. Completion of processing does not save a file automatically.
  2. Play the saved file, including the end, and check the subject, captions, orientation and sound.
  3. Open it in your destination app and check its current resolution, duration and size requirements.

Re-encoding can change image quality and file size. Extra subtitles, HDR appearance and metadata are not guaranteed to survive. Multiple video or audio tracks are rejected; use a desktop editor for those projects.

Try a known sample

Download the four-second test clip with four colored regions, a moving marker and a steady tone. Use it to check the selected frame before choosing private footage.

The first two outputs came from the four-color source above. The third used our six-second silent portrait source, with the network disconnected during processing. All three downloaded outputs fully decoded and had the expected dimensions. The two colored crops were independently compared with the matching source rectangles; this verifies these sample regions, not every source or browser.

If a video cannot be cropped

If the preview cannot load, try a complete H.264 MP4 export or open the original in a desktop editor. Browser codec support varies. A file extension alone does not show which video and audio codecs it contains.

Use one video track and at most one audio track, up to 250 MB. Available memory can impose a smaller practical limit. Cancel stops an active job and leaves the original unchanged. An unsupported encoder or failed output check produces an error instead of a partial download.

Continue editing

Need a smaller file? Use the video compressor. To combine several edits, follow the short silent portrait MP4 example. Need another file format? Convert to MP4 or WebM. For a short silent loop, use video to GIF. For Canva generation and export, follow the Canva AI video guide.

Processing and test scope

The tool uses self-hosted Mediabunny and the browser's media codecs. MPL-2.0 license · Original source package. Video content is not sent to a cropping server. No account is required and the tool adds no watermark.

Shared samples cover a bounded desktop Chromium test on November 25, 2026. They do not establish support for every device, rotated source or video codec. This tool does not add missing detail, change video length or follow a moving subject.
